pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/simhash.rs:402 Persisted record fingerprints depend on hash_token's exact output, an unpromised and load-bearing regularity. Its stability is stated only in this comment and in the manual `reindex_simhashes` one-shot (datasets.rs:2317). No test pins a known fingerprint value and no algorithm marker is stored, so a future edit to the token hash (as the later splitmix finalizer was) ships green and silently mixes incomparable fingerprints in the store.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/simhash.rs:516 The simhash tests assert only relative Hamming distances (near/far/zero). All of them would still pass if hash_token changed, so the persisted-fingerprint regularity is true but not tested. The publisher-side aid is a manual reindex (datasets.rs:2317), with no probe that detects a mixed store.

pairs.registryProposal: announcing-versus-silent-breakage frames the silent class as release-to-consumer. A sibling case is worth naming: a producer's own persisted derived values (fingerprints, content hashes) are a silent contract with the producer's past self. There the aid is a stored algorithm-version marker or a golden-value test, not a restore switch.

pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:706 The scheduler added a seventh member, `retired`, to the existing `health` string that GET /schedules publishes. The schema field's contract text (crates/server/src/routes/dto.rs:373, and so openapi.json and the generated TS/CLI types) still enumerates only six values. The route description lists seven, so readers built from the field schema were never told about the new member of an existing shape.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:706 A new member went through an existing shape (blast radius: every reader of `health`) without the contract's member list being fixed in the same change (commit 72eed87, typed `feat`, not breaking). Health is an untyped Option<String>, so derived readers cannot see the vocabulary at all.
